issues.legal_issue: An administrative authority cannot review its final order rejecting a revision application when it has no express statutory power of review.
material_facts: A party applied to the State authority for revision of an order concerning land allotments.
The authority rejected the revision application, then later reconsidered the same application, heard the parties, and allowed it.
The governing Act contained no express power authorising review of an order made on a revision application.
issues.conclusion: The authority lacked jurisdiction to review its earlier rejection, so its later order allowing the revision was ultra vires and was rightly quashed by the High Court.
issues.legal_principle: Section 42 of the East Punjab Holdings (Consolidation and Prevention of Fragmentation) Act, 1948 empowered the State Government to examine specified records and pass orders, but did not expressly confer a power to review an order made under that section. A final order cannot be set aside or reviewed by the authority that made it unless statute grants that power. The Court relied on Drew v. Willis, Hession v. Jones, Anantharaju Shetty v. Appu Hegada, and Baijnath Ram Goenka v. Nand Kumar Singh, and followed Patel Chunibhai Dajibhai v. Narayanrao Khanderao Jambekar. The High Court could quash the jurisdictionally invalid order under Article 226 of the Constitution.

rule.if: revision_proceeding and earlier_final_rejection and later_reconsideration and no_express_review_power

predicates.revision_proceeding: A party invoked an authority's revisional jurisdiction to challenge an earlier decision.
predicates.earlier_final_rejection: The authority made a final order rejecting the revision application.
predicates.later_reconsideration: The authority later reopened and reconsidered the same revision application.
predicates.no_express_review_power: The governing law did not expressly authorise the authority to review its final order.
predicates.later_review_order_invalid: A later order reopening and changing the final rejection is beyond the authority's jurisdiction.

issues.definition: When a revision proceeding has been finally rejected, the authority later reconsiders it, and the governing law gives no express review power, the later review order is invalid.
